statements.text: The Prime Minister is set to tell President Zelenskyy that he has asked Ministers to draw up further sanctions, military support and fiscal packages to provide urgent support in the coming weeks. The UK will accelerate deliveries of Lightweight Multirole Missiles, which it says have proven extremely effective against jet-powered drones. The UK has committed £1.6 billion to deliver more than 5,000 of these missiles to Ukraine over four years, and will accelerate £10 million of a £45 million missile package for Ukraine's most urgent winter needs. On 14 October, at Downing Street, the Prime Minister set out the UK's latest package of these missiles.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said that UK support for Ukraine is vital for keeping the UK safe and for ensuring those on the frontlines have the equipment to push back Russia, that the UK is with Ukraine for as long as it takes and will go further and faster, that this support is not just the right thing but the necessary thing to do, and that Russia's aggression cannot be allowed to succeed on the continent.

The Prime Minister told the Commons on 12 October that he welcomed President Trump's announcement of a reciprocal energy ceasefire. He said President Zelenskyy has assured him Ukraine would immediately implement a reciprocal energy ceasefire once a start date is confirmed, and that he will discuss this further with President Zelenskyy in the coming days.

The Prime Minister told the Commons on 12 October that new funding has been announced to help Ukraine get through its fifth winter under Russian bombardment, and that a new sanctions package means over 90% of Russia's oil producing capacity is now covered by UK sanctions.

The Prime Minister told the Commons on 12 October that the government's assessment is that the incident at RAF Fairford is highly likely to have been coordinated in Iran and almost certainly directed by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. He said the UK will not tolerate these threats on its soil, will crack down on Iran's use of criminal networks, and will bring further sanctions to restrict Iran and the IRGC's capacity to do harm.

The Prime Minister told the Commons on 12 October that the UK-EU summit will take place in Brussels on 20 November. On the table are a trade deal on food and drink products, an emissions trading agreement, progress towards linking energy systems, a new youth experience scheme and deeper cooperation on immigration.

The Prime Minister said a trade deal on food and drink is projected to add over £10 billion a year to the UK economy by 2040, with potential to add significantly more. He said it would lift a burden that can reach £1,400 on a single shipment for farmers and food producers, and would mean no more export health certificates, which can cost up to £200 each time, for small businesses.

The Prime Minister told the Commons on 12 October that he believes the UK's chances of a summit deal will be enhanced by being open to discussing the relationship with the EU in the longer term. He said the immediate priority is a successful outcome at the summit, after which he believes a serious dialogue should be set up about the options for the long-term relationship.

In a speech on 15 October the Prime Minister invited Scotland's First Minister to work with him to push more power out of Westminster and Holyrood. He said the UK Government, through No10 North and the Scotland Office, will call on the Scottish Government to develop a new model of regional empowerment for Scotland, and said he is making a serious and genuine offer to the Scottish Government.

Andy Burnham said he is making an offer to the Scottish Government, having told the First Minister in his first week in office that he wanted to work with him. Douglas Alexander said the Prime Minister's offer is what he called a genuine one, and that the Scotland Office is ready to work alongside the Scottish Government to make it happen.

The site of Great British Railways' headquarters was unveiled in Derby on 15 October 2026, at Becketwell, a brownfield site in Derby city centre. Construction is expected to begin in early 2027 and be completed by spring 2029. The HQ is estimated to bring a £151 million boost to Derby's economy and hundreds of rail jobs, and will accommodate up to 450 GBR staff.

Andy Burnham said that for too long people have put up with a railway that often lets them down, and that today is another big step forward. Heidi Alexander said the biggest shake-up to the railways in a generation is underway, with Great British Railways bringing the railway together around better services for passengers. Up to 600 apprentices aged 16 to 21 will enrol over the next four years on the rail foundation apprenticeship.

On 15 October the King appointed William James Baxter QPM DL as Lord-Lieutenant of County Tyrone, succeeding Sir Robert William Lowry Scott following his retirement on 17 June 2026. Baxter served in the RUC/PSNI from 1973 until 2003, and was District Commander in Omagh in 1997, including on the day of the Omagh bombing in 1998.

The Prime Minister told the Commons on 12 October that the UK has decided to send air defence and a Voyager aircraft to Saudi Arabia to provide air-to-air refuelling support, and confirmed a Voyager has already completed 14 operational missions. He condemned the appalling attacks on King Khalid International Airport.

speakers: Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey
statements.text: Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey said he urges partners to back the ban on Russian LNG, like the UK has done, to curtail the war chest funding Putin, and the Chancellor is urging partners at the IMF meetings in Bangkok to fully implement an equivalent ban.

In his Motherwell speech on 16 October the Prime Minister said the Scottish Government has agreed this week to match the UK Government's £10 million to create two defence technical excellence colleges, one in the east and one in the west of Scotland.

In his Motherwell speech on 16 October the Prime Minister offered Scotland DWP devolution, a model of localised employment support similar to the one in England but shaped by Holyrood and right for Scotland.

In his Motherwell speech on 16 October the Prime Minister said the National Economic Council will meet in a couple of weeks with the First Ministers of Scotland and Wales and the First Minister and Deputy First Minister of Northern Ireland, the first such meeting since he became Prime Minister, to put the offer on the table and see if a plan can be worked out together.
